translations.text: It is fitting to commemorate the holy, spotless and valiant archpriest and martyr,
to whom the throne of glory was justly granted because of his great faith and because of his witness to the truth, [attested] by all,
who offered himself as a sacrifice for the One who offered himself to the Father and bought us with his own blood,

who, with the help of the Most High, brought forth fruits from himself: the sixtyfold of holiness and the hundredfold of ascetic struggle. By uniting the sevenfold with himself, he became the one who brings these to completion, the archpriest of the Most High,
the mediator between God and humankind, the blessed Abibos, bishop of the city of Nekresi.
For he stood forth between two holy ranks. Among his fellow priests he held the throne of the priesthood through his blameless priesthood and his right dividing [of the word of truth],
and among the martyrs again, through his valiant struggle, he was honored with two crowns in the ranks of the righteous.
This martyr and spotless archpriest is mine: a beautiful fruit who brings gladness to us and spreads our fragrance to us,
a lamp burning on high, a luminary who gives light to all, to all of his own, who spotlessly offered the body and blood of Christ,
and who also offered himself to Him as a sacrifice, at the hand of the lawless marzpan.
The cause of his martyrdom was as follows.
At that time this kingdom of ours, Kartli, had been seized by the king of the Persians, and they were practicing their foul worship, as they had been wickedly taught by their teacher, the devil.
Because of this they set up many places in this land of ours for their worship, and they led astray many who were not firm in the faith and were lacking in understanding.
But the blessed Abibos, bishop of the city of Nekresi in the principality of Kakheti,
was stirred to earnest action by divine zeal. He went up close to their foreign place of worship, poured water on it, and put out that [?] god, their fire.
When the lawless Persians learned of this, they seized him and beat him so badly that the blessed man was thought to be close to death. Afterwards they shut him up in prison in great distress.
After much torture they wrote to the upper country, to their king's marzpan, and he sent orders that they should quickly bring him before him in chains.
The envoys came and took the holy Abibos away, and he traveled with them through many kinds of hardship.
Now this blessed bishop was a friend of that brilliant luminary, Symeon the Stylite of Antioch. They had never seen each other with their eyes,
but through spiritual love, by which someone far away is seen in the mind as if near, and also through letters and messengers, they had come to know each other.
And at the very time when the holy Abibos was being taken away, a messenger of the blessed Symeon the Stylite met him in a village
called Ialdos. He gave him a letter, a eulogia (blessing) and the staff of our holy father Symeon the wonderworker.
When the bishop received the eulogia and the staff and read the saint's letter, he rejoiced with great joy and was greatly strengthened.
After this some people met him and said: "If you do not wish to go on, we will take you back to your home."
But he refused, for he longed to be martyred for Christ.
And when they reached the royal city of Mtskheta, he called in supplication upon the holy catholic and apostolic Church, and said:
"Your son Joseph goes to Egypt bound, like a captive. And how could anyone have said to him:
'Not so; rather, you are being prepared to reign, and your sending is from the heavenly dwellings'? So may I too go on this way in peace."
Then the blessed one begged those torturers that he might go [?]......
But none of the beasts or birds touched the body of the thrice-blessed holy struggler, and as though [?] they were guarding it, they left it and went away.
Then those who lived in the cave came, the place where those same holy men had built a monastery as a dwelling, and they took up the relics of Saint Abibos
and buried them with great honour in that place. And so the blessed Abibos was offered up to God like a sacrificial gift, a fragrant offering,
like the father of the great Zacharias, to whom the lot of the high priesthood had fallen; and like him, he too shed his holy blood for our Lord.
... I am not telling you about all of his struggle in this account of the martyrdom of the blessed bishop Abibos.
I am not telling you about all his deeds and labours, or how he smashed the idols, brought the godless to believe in Christ, and baptized them in the name of the Holy Trinity,
or how he also foretold to that woman that the Greeks would come after him and conquer this land of ours, which indeed soon came to pass.
While that same woman was still alive, the Greeks came, drove out those lawless Persians, and conquered this land of ours.
From then on, eristavis (dukes) became the rulers of Kartli.
And there are many other deeds and wonders of this saint that are not written in this book of his martyrdom.
But look and understand wisely, beloved of Christ, what kind of men they were and how great: holy men, wholly pleasing to God, lights of the world,
chosen vessels filled with fragrant ointment, heavenly men and earthly angels, enlighteners of the world,
models, rules and unerring canons of monastic life, [?] in this land......
At one time there appeared [?]......, and they bore his holy commandments, guided by a virtuous way of life.
And this same land of ours became blessed by being the treasury of their holy relics.
And now, beloved brothers, let us pray and ask Christ God that, through their holy prayers and intercession, he may make us worthy to imitate their virtues
and to glorify the Holy Trinity forever, to whom honour and worship are fitting, now and always and to the ages of ages. Amen.
